extracted.intended_audience: established biomedical researchers considering applying to the HHMI Investigator Program (and host-institution research administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection philosophy for appointment as a Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) Investigator: describes the qualities, expectations, and procedural terms HHMI looks for when selecting and supporting investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: People, not projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Our philosophy of selecting “people, not projects” seeks researchers who bring innovative approaches to the study of many different biological problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI emphasizes evaluating the investigator (their creativity, judgment, and long-term potential) rather than a single specific project. Funding is long-term and flexible to allow investigators freedom to explore and change direction; investigators are supported to follow their ideas through to fruition even if that process takes a very long time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity and productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 324 Howard Hughes Medical Institute investigators, widely known for their creativity and productivity, are pushing the bounds of knowledge in biomedical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to have a strong record of creative, productive research. HHMI highlights both past productivity and the capacity to drive novel work forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to take risks and explore unproven avenues
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI urges its researchers to take risks, explore unproven avenues, and embrace the unknown – even if it means uncertainty or the chance of failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for investigators who pursue high-risk/high-reward directions; tolerance for uncertainty and possible failure is an explicit positive attribute in selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and pursuit of significant biological questions with rigor and depth
rubrics_metrics.description: They identify and pursue significant biological questions in a rigorous and deep manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators look for investigators who choose important problems and address them with sustained, rigorous scientific approaches rather than superficial or incremental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of new tools, methods, and interdisciplinary techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: They develop new tools and methods that enable creative experimental approaches to biological questions, when necessary bringing to bear concepts or techniques from other disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of methodological innovation and ability to integrate techniques/concepts from other fields (e.g., biophysics, chemical biology, engineering, computation) is valued as enabling novel experiments and discoveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative approaches across biomedical and adjacent fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Our philosophy seeks researchers who bring innovative approaches to the study of many different biological problems through the biomedical disciplines of genetics, cell biology, developmental biology, biochemistry, and neuroscience as well as adjacent fields of biophysics, chemical biology, biomedical engineering, and computational biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI favors investigators whose work spans or connects traditional disciplines and who apply novel conceptual approaches to biological problems; diversity of disciplinary perspective is a positive attribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational linkage: forging links between basic biology and medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: They forge links between basic biology and medicine, opening new pathways for disease diagnosis and drug discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While HHMI emphasizes basic research, investigators who create plausible pathways from fundamental discoveries to medical or translational impact are highlighted positively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to make significant contributions to science
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI accepts applications ... with the aim of identifying individuals who have the potential to make significant contributions to science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasizes future impact potential as well as past accomplishments — candidates should demonstrate trajectories or ideas suggesting major future contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with host institution responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators continue to participate in educational and administrative activities at their host institutions and receive additional research support from a variety of sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI expects investigators to maintain roles at their host institutions (teaching, administration, mentoring) alongside HHMI-supported research, indicating capacity to balance institutional duties with independent research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment terms and review (procedural expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each investigator receives his or her full salary, benefits, and a research budget from HHMI. Appointment is for a five-year term, which may be renewed after an exacting review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should understand the institutional/administrative terms: HHMI appointments are five-year HHMI-supported positions with renewal contingent on rigorous review of performance and progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHMI Collaborative Innovation Awards (HCIA) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: HCIA support interdisciplinary teams of scientists, each headed by an HHMI investigator, in pursuing potentially transformative research projects; intended to encourage HHMI investigators to collaborate with scientists, both inside and outside of HHMI, to undertake projects that are new and so large in scope that they require a team with a range of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitive HCIA proposals should be led by an HHMI investigator, be interdisciplinary, target transformative aims, and justify large team-based scope; collaborators receive HHMI funding for the HCIA project (four years) and awards are made after HHMI invites investigators to propose collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHMI–GBMF plant investigator emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI investigators include some of the nation’s most innovative plant scientists, appointed ... through a partnership between HHMI and the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation (GBMF). These 14 HHMI-GBMF investigators are conducting research on a variety of plants, such as wheat, maize, tomato, Arabidopsis, moss, and algae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the GBMF partnership, HHMI specifically seeks creative plant biologists to pursue bold research with potential large contributions to science and society; this represents a targeted emphasis on underfunded areas within plant science.
